newsitem.title: FRANCE: Channel Tunnel fire may have been foul play - firm.
newsitem.headline: Channel Tunnel fire may have been foul play - firm.

text.p: A French magistrate investigating a fire that seriously damaged the Channel Tunnel last week has not ruled out foul play as a possible cause, a spokeswoman for the rail link's operator, Eurotunnel SA/Plc said on Wednesday.

"The judge has not ruled out the theory of foul play," a company spokeswoman told Reuters. Justice sources said the idea that the fire was set deliberately aboard a truck shuttle was regarded as a remote possibility and not the most likely cause.

On Monday, a British member of parliament for the Channel port of Dover, David Shaw, asked Transport Secretary Sir George Young in the House of Commons whether he was aware of allegations that the blaze "was sabotage by a striking French lorry driver".
Young replied: "I know that the French inquiry...that is under way will want to look at the cause of the fire and will want to look at the allegations that (Shaw) mentions."

The fire occurred on November 18, just after French truck drivers had begun a strike for higher pay, shorter working hours and earlier retirement. They have gradually blockaded many highways, ports and borders.

Witnesses said a lorry carrying inflammable polystyrene was seen on fire before the shuttle train entered the tunnel. Eurotunnel's French co-chairman, Patrick Ponsolle, told Europe 1 radio that no possible cause could be ruled out.
